papers.title: Ermakov--Based embeddings as a parameter-free layer for physics-informed neural networks
papers.summary: Evolution equations with time-dependent coefficients force a neural solver to spend capacity on a scale that the equation already determines. We show that a single classical object, the Ermakov-Pinney scale function $\rho$, can be written into the input layer of a physics-informed neural network as a parameter-free embedding. One construction covers three problem families through the two signs of the Pinney constant $c$: linear diffusion ($c=-1$, $\omega\equiv0$), diffusion in a time-dependent confining trap ($c=-1$, $\omega\neq0$), and the quantum oscillator with time-dependent frequency ($c=+1$). An exact moment identity gives $\rho$ in closed form from the initial data alone, so no auxiliary network or knowledge of the solution is needed. Our central finding is comparative: each family requires a different component of the construction and has a different honest control. In family I, the diffusive-time reparametrisation alone reproduces most of the gain, so that family is a poor test of the idea and shows why an ablation is mandatory. In family II no time reparametrisation exists, the control degrades accuracy, and the amplitude prefactor becomes essential (40.8x). In family III the adiabatic approximation also fails, and the quadratic phase factor is what matters (5.7x). The method does not help when the reduced solution does not converge to a fixed point: its extrapolation advantage then disappears. The reduction itself is the classical scaling-variable change of the self-similar-asymptotics literature; what is new is the moment identity that makes it architectural for time-dependent coefficients, and the comparative anatomy above.
papers.title_ja: 物理情報ニューラルネットワークにおけるパラメータフリー層としての Ermakov ベース埋め込み
papers.summary_ja: 時間依存係数を持つ進化方程式を解く物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）において、Ermakov-Pinney スケール関数を用いたパラメータフリーな埋め込み手法を提案する。初期データのみから閉形式で得られるこの関数を入力層に組み込むことで、線形拡散、時間依存トラップ内拡散、量子振動子の3つの問題系で精度向上を実証した。比較分析により、各問題系で効く構成要素（時間再パラメータ化、振幅係数、二次位相因子）が異なり、特に時間再パラメータ化が存在しない系では振幅係数が40.8倍の改善をもたらすことを示した。この手法は、解が固定点に収束しない場合の外挿優位性が失われるという限界も明確にしている。

papers.title: Physics-Informed Identification of Tensegrity Prestress across Taut-Slack Transitions
papers.summary: Prestress governs the stability, stiffness, and dynamic behavior of tensegrity structures, but it is not directly observable from sparse structural measurements, and it may decrease during service life. Under strong excitation, the cables may slacken and the dynamics become nonsmooth. Existing identification methods are limited to the taut regime, and physics-informed networks for tensegrities solve only the forward problem of predicting the response from known member parameters. This study formulates the inverse problem. Neural networks are trained on the equation-of-motion residual in constrained Cartesian coordinates, where the mass matrix is constant and the force densities enter linearly. The force densities, damping, and axial stiffness are trainable parameters, and the tension-only cable law is kept. A Fisher-information analysis shows, before inversion, which member parameters a record can determine. The method is tested on simulated planar tensegrity frames with up to five modules and a three-dimensional prism, and on measured records of a biomimetic leg and a full-scale tensegrity simplex. On the one-module frame, the identifiable force densities are recovered within 1.5% from noisy accelerations at half the free coordinates, on records with and without taut-slack transitions. Records with transitions determine members that taut records leave undetermined. On the five-module frame, a 16-cable two-span bridge, the median force-density error rises moderately, to 4.2%. On measured records, an identified spring stiffness is within 0.1% of its independently measured value on average, and the identified simplex prestress at 13 levels agrees with its cable force transducers to 2.9% root-mean-square.
papers.title_ja: 緊張構造の張力-弛緩遷移における物理情報に基づくプレストレス同定
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、緊張構造（テンセグリティ）におけるプレストレスを逆問題として同定する物理情報ニューラルネットワーク（PINN）手法を提案する。運動方程式の残差を損失関数に用いることで、ケーブルの張力密度や減衰係数などのパラメータを推定可能とし、従来の手法では扱えなかったケーブルの弛緩（タウト-スラック）遷移を含む非滑らかな動的挙動にも対応する。シミュレーションおよび実測データを用いた検証により、ノイズの多い加速度データから高精度でプレストレスを復元できることを示し、特に遷移を含む記録が同定不能なパラメータの決定に有効であることを明らかにした。
papers.relevance_reason: 物理情報ニューラルネットと構造力学の逆問題解決という、ユーザーの関心領域に完全に一致する手法。

papers.title: SCANO: Restoring Boundary-Condition Completeness in Sampled Meshes with a Sliced-Cross-Attention Neural Operator for 3D Thermal Fields
papers.summary: Training neural operators on million-cell meshes can exceed GPU memory limits. Models are therefore trained on subsamples and deployed on whole meshes or selected regions. However, subsampling can distort boundary information, degrading accuracy. We ask when boundary conditioning under sampling stays consistent with whole-mesh training, and how to aggregate and inject boundary data. Representing the solution as an integral of boundary data against type-dependent measures, we show that subsampling distorts this conditioning in three ways: incomplete boundary coverage or a sample-dependent global state, face weighting by count rather than area, and compression of boundary inputs into a low-dimensional vector. This analysis yields four measurable consistency conditions checkable before training. We satisfy them with two backbone-agnostic modules. Boundary Quadrature Attention (BQA) aggregates all boundary faces, typed and area-weighted, into slice tokens that every query point reads at every layer. Anchored Global State (AGS) estimates the global state from anchors independent of the sampled points. Adding both to a scalable message-passing and slice-attention backbone yields SCANO. We evaluate the approach on controlled and public benchmarks and a data-centre thermal simulation dataset (DCTS) containing million-cell meshes. On both benchmarks, BQA improves every backbone, reducing whole-mesh error up to 15-fold. On all three datasets, AGS aligns regional with whole-mesh predictions, cutting regional error at least tenfold for most backbones on the public benchmark. Together, the modules nearly halve the best original backbone's whole-mesh error on both benchmarks. SCANO predicts a room-scale field in under one second, over 100 times faster than whole-room anchor self-attention.
papers.title_ja: SCANO: 3D熱場におけるサンプリングメッシュの境界条件完全性をスライスト・クロスアテンション・ニューラルオペレータで復元する手法
papers.summary_ja: 大規模メッシュでのニューラルオペレータ学習時のGPUメモリ制約と、サブサンプリングによる境界情報の歪みを解決する手法を提案する。境界データを面積重み付きで集約するBQAと、サンプリング点に依存しないグローバル状態を推定するAGSという2つのモジュールを導入し、境界条件の一貫性を保証する。これにより、数百万セルのデータセンター熱シミュレーションにおいて、全体メッシュのエラーを最大15倍、地域別エラーを10倍以上低減し、1秒未満で予測を実現した。

papers.title: Deep Neural Operator Learning for stochastic heat equations and applications
papers.summary: In this paper, we establish a universal approximation theorem for solution operators of semilinear stochastic heat equations in spatial dimension \(d\ge2\), extending deep neural operator approximation results to SPDEs with distribution-valued Gaussian forcing. A smooth Fourier cutoff reduces the forcing to finitely many measurements, while Besov and Schauder estimates control the resulting solution error. The finite-dimensional solution map is then approximated by ReLU branch networks together with grid-based trunk functions, yielding explicit bounds on the numbers of forcing measurements and trunk functions and approximation in every finite stochastic moment. For linear equations, the reduction coincides with truncation of the first Wiener chaos. Lastly, as an application, we prove a high-probability local-in-time approximation theorem for stochastic Navier--Stokes equations, with finite measurements of both the initial condition and forcing and an explicit sensing rate.
papers.title_ja: 確率熱方程式およびその応用における深層ニューラルオペレータ学習
papers.summary_ja: 空間次元2以上の半線形確率熱方程式の解演算子に対する汎用近似定理を確立した。フーリエカットオフによりガウス強制を有限測定に削減し、ReLUブランチネットワークとグリッドベーストランク関数による近似誤差の明示的上界を導出した。さらに、確率ナビエ・ストークス方程式に対する高確率な時間局所近似定理を証明し、初期条件と強制の有限測定から得られる明示的なセンシングレートを示した。
papers.relevance_reason: ニューラルオペレータと物理情報モデルの理論的基盤を強化する重要論文

papers.title: Macrocanonical Generator Networks: Data-Efficient Neural Surrogates for Amortized Physics Simulation
papers.summary: Many scientific simulations are computationally expensive, limiting their use in simulation-based inference, uncertainty quantification, and decision making. We introduce macrocanonical generator networks, a framework for learning fast, data-efficient neural surrogates for amortized simulation of stationary physical processes by matching multiscale statistics of a target process. Inspired by microcanonical maximum-entropy synthesis, which matches feature statistics per sample by inner-loop optimization, our approach instead trains a neural generator to satisfy the same constraints in expectation, preserving physically realistic sample-to-sample fluctuations. We prove that gradient-descent training induces preconditioned gradient-descent dynamics in sample space that inherit the symmetry-preservation properties of the microcanonical gradient descent of Bruna and Mallat, amortizing its per-sample inner-loop optimization into a single training run after which every sample is generated in one forward pass. We further show that residual generator parameterizations initialized near the identity, trained with a small learning rate, preserve entropy locally during early optimization and mitigate mode collapse. Experiments on cosmology and fluid simulations show that macrocanonical generators recover realistic samples from extremely small training sets, in some cases a single training example, while generating new realizations more than $10^6$ times faster per sample than the reference simulator and more than $10^3$ times faster than microcanonical gradient descent. The trained generators can be reused for downstream pretraining, including simulation-based inference, providing a data-efficient route to multi-fidelity scientific machine learning workflows.
papers.title_ja: 巨視的生成ネットワーク：償却物理シミュレーションのためのデータ効率の良いニューラルサロゲート
papers.summary_ja: 計算コストの高い物理シミュレーションを高速化するため、巨視的生成ネットワークというニューラルサロゲートモデルを提案する。微正則最大エントロピー合成の統計制約を期待値で満たすよう学習することで、サンプルごとの内部ループ最適化を単一の学習プロセスに集約し、1回のフォワードパスでリアルなサンプルを生成する。宇宙論や流体シミュレーションにおいて、極めて少ない学習データ（場合によっては1サンプル）から現実的な分布を再現し、参照シミュレータ比で100万倍以上の高速化を実現した。この手法は、シミュレーションベース推論や不確実性定量化など、データ効率の低い科学計算ワークフローへの応用が期待される。

papers.title: AgentAM: An AI Agent for Spatter- and Defect-Aware Process Optimization in Laser Powder Bed Fusion
papers.summary: Predictive models for laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) are rarely used on the shop floor because querying them requires programming and model-specific knowledge. We present AgentAM, a large language model (LLM) agent that gives process engineers natural-language access to CFD-trained surrogates of spatter and melt pool geometry for SS316L through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Polynomial surrogates trained on 279 single-track simulations predict melt pool dimensions ($R^2 \geq 0.95$) and spatter volume ($R^2 = 0.83$ on test data) at any power-velocity point in the trained range, and geometric criteria assign each point a geometry-derived defect regime (keyhole, lack of fusion, balling or stable) that matches the regime obtained from the simulated geometry in 93.4% of tracks under cross-validation. The agent selects and parameterizes tools for prediction, process-window scans and constrained optimization. Minimum-spatter optima often sat within 10 $\mu$m of the lack-of-fusion boundary; a margin-aware optimizer moved them away from all thresholds and raised the estimated probability of remaining classified Good from 0.94 to 1.00 under an assumed 2% process drift, and from 0.72 to 0.91 when jointly sampled cross-validated geometry residuals were added. About 40-50 well-spread simulations sufficed to reproduce the defect map. To evaluate the agent layer, we introduce a 145-prompt benchmark scored against direct tool calls, plus eight prompts (40 runs) on margin-aware requests. Over the 725 runs of the main benchmark the agent passed the intended inputs in 98.5% of parsing prompts, reported the scored spatter values and defect classes faithfully and met every stated constraint in the 65 feasible optimization runs, within a median 1.0% of the brute-force optimum.
papers.title_ja: AgentAM: レーザー粉末床溶融積層における飛散・欠陥認識プロセス最適化のためのAIエージェント
papers.summary_ja: 本論文は、LLMエージェントを用いてCFD訓練されたサロゲートモデル（多項式近似）に自然言語でアクセスし、レーザー粉末床溶融積層（LPBF）のプロセス最適化を行うフレームワークを提案する。279回のシミュレーションから訓練されたサロゲートは、溶融プール寸法と飛散体積を高精度に予測し、欠陥レジームの分類も93.4%の一致率を示した。さらに、マージン認識型最適化により、欠陥境界からの距離を確保しつつ飛散を最小化するパラメータを特定し、プロセスドリフト下での品質維持確率を向上させた。最後に、エージェントのツール呼び出し精度と最適化性能を評価する145プロンプトのベンチマークを構築し、98.5%の入力解析成功率と最適解に近い結果を得たことを報告している。

papers.title: Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems
papers.summary: Model reduction via the Mori-Zwanzig (MZ) formalism is well understood for coarse-grained representations constructed from standard basis functions such as Fourier functions. We show that the same formalism can be used to build reduced-order models in bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning. The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) is used to close the resulting non-Markovian evolution equations for the expansion coefficients of the learned basis. We further introduce a complementary, generative closure model. Relative to the Markovian dynamics alone, both the MZ and generative closures substantially improve predictions of the filtered states.
papers.title_ja: 多スケール系のための物理情報付き伝統的および生成型Mori-Zwanzig縮約モデル
papers.summary_ja: Mori-Zwanzig（MZ）形式を用いた縮約モデル構築において、物理情報機械学習で発見された基底関数への適用可能性を示した。波動散逸定理（FDT）を用いて非マルコフ進化方程式を閉じ、さらに補完的な生成型クローズチャモデルを提案した。マルコフ動力学のみと比較し、これら2つのクローズチャ手法がフィルタリング状態の予測精度を大幅に向上させることを実証した。
